roleDesc.sweeper-keeper: A goalkeeper who sweeps up balls behind the defensive line and initiates counter-attacks with long distribution.
roleDesc.goalkeeper: The standard goalkeeper role. Stays between the sticks, organizes the defense, and makes saves.
roleDesc.ball-playing-defender: A center-back who builds play from the back with accurate passing and composure under pressure.
roleDesc.central-defender: The traditional no-nonsense defender. Wins aerial duels and makes crucial tackles.
roleDesc.full-back: Balanced wide defender who supports both attack and defense from the flanks.
roleDesc.wing-back: An attacking-minded wide player who provides the main source of width in formations without wingers.
roleDesc.deep-lying-playmaker: A midfield orchestrator who dictates tempo from deep positions with incisive passing range.
roleDesc.box-to-box-midfielder: An energetic midfielder who contributes at both ends of the pitch with relentless running.
roleDesc.advanced-playmaker: The creative hub operating between the lines, threading through balls and unlocking defenses.
roleDesc.inside-forward: Cuts inside from wide positions to score goals, acting more like a striker than a traditional winger.
roleDesc.advanced-forward: The primary goal-scoring outlet who plays on the shoulder of the last defender.
roleDesc.pressing-forward: A defensive forward who harasses opposition defenders and forces mistakes high up the pitch.
roleDesc.target-forward: A physical presence who holds up the ball and brings teammates into play with knock-downs and layoffs.
roleDesc.line-holding-keeper: A traditional goalkeeper introduced in FM26 who holds his line and stays deep — ideal for defences that sit back and protect the box.
roleDesc.overlapping-centre-back: A FM26 centre-back role for three-at-the-back systems who steps out and overlaps on the flank, adding an extra body in the final third.
roleDesc.playmaking-wing-back: The advanced FM26 wing-back role that drifts inside to dictate play, creating overloads while the wide forward stretches the pitch.
roleDesc.channel-midfielder: A new FM26 midfielder who attacks the half-spaces between the lines, arriving late in the box and combining between midfield and attack.

Modern sweeper keeper who excels at sweeping behind a high line and starting attacks with long passes.
Top-tier reactions and 1v1s with genuine command of the area — ready-made for the top leagues now.

formations.heroSubtitle: Complete guide to Football Manager 2026 formations. Each formation is broken down with strengths, weaknesses, recommended roles, and the best tactical styles — so you can pick the right shape for your squad.
formations.faqQ1: What is the best formation in FM26?
formations.faqA1: The best FM26 formation depends on your play style. The 4-2-3-1 is the most balanced and great for gegenpress, the 4-3-3 is ideal for tiki-taka and possession, the 4-4-2 is excellent for counter-attacking and wing play, and the 3-5-2 is perfect for defensive/counter-attacking teams.
formations.faqQ2: How do I choose the right formation in Football Manager 2026?
formations.faqA2: Consider your squad's strengths: if you have strong wingers, use 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1; if you have dominant CBs and athletic wing-backs, try 3-5-2; for counter-attacking with limited players, 4-4-2 or 5-3-2 work best. Always match the formation to your players' attributes.
formations.faqQ3: What formation is best for underdogs in FM26?
formations.faqA3: The 4-4-2 and 5-3-2 are the best formations for underdogs and smaller clubs in FM26. They provide solid defensive structures with two banks of players, making them hard to break down while still offering counter-attacking threat through two strikers.

4-2-3-1.description: The modern classic. Two holding midfielders support a creative attacking midfielder with wingers providing width.
4-2-3-1.bestFor: Balanced attacking play with a strong defensive shield
weaknesses: Can be overrun in midfield against 4-3-3

4-3-3.description: Wide forwards stretch the opposition. Three midfielders offer balance between defense and attack.
weaknesses: Can be exposed on the counter

4-4-2.description: The traditional English setup. Two banks of four with a classic strike partnership.
strengths: Two banks of four = solid defense

3-5-2.description: Wing-backs provide width as three center-backs form a solid defensive base with two strikers.
3-5-2.bestFor: Counter-attacking with defensive solidity (Catenaccio, Low Block)
weaknesses: Vulnerable out wide if wing-backs caught up

5-3-2.description: Ultra-defensive shape with wing-backs. Counter-attack specialist formation.
strengths: Five defenders = very hard to break down

3-4-3.description: Attacking formation with wing-backs pushing high. Three forwards apply constant pressure on opposing defenders.
3-4-3.bestFor: Aggressive attacking football with high wing-backs

4-2-2-2.description: Brazilian Box. Two DMs and two AMs create a compact midfield box, with two strikers leading the line.
4-2-2-2.bestFor: Box midfield control and attacking flair
weaknesses: Can be predictable through the middle

4-1-4-1.description: A solid DM shields the back four. Four midfielders offer width and numbers in the middle third.
4-1-4-1.bestFor: Defensive stability with a dedicated DM shield

4-4-1-1.description: The Mourinho special. A second striker or #10 operates between the lines behind a lone target man.
4-4-1-1.bestFor: Counter-attacking with a #10 behind a target man

5-2-3.description: Three center-backs with attacking wing-backs. Wide forwards stretch play and create overloads in the final third.

4-2-4.description: Ultra-attacking shape with four forwards. Risky but devastating — the FM26 community's top-scoring formation in tests.
4-2-4.bestFor: All-out attack when you need goals

3-4-2-1.description: Conte's trademark. Two #10s behind a lone striker with wing-backs providing width. Extremely solid through the middle.
3-4-2-1.bestFor: Defensive solidity with two playmakers behind a striker

4-3-2-1.description: Christmas Tree. Narrow and compact. Two advanced playmakers operate behind a solo striker, overwhelming the opponent's midfield.

4-1-2-1-2.description: Diamond midfield. A DM anchors, two CMs shuttle, and a #10 creates. Two strikers give you vertical threat against any back line.
4-1-2-1-2.bestFor: Vertical attacking threat with two strikers
